EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

usage_disposition.description: Whether `usage` was provider-reported or the attempt ended before the provider's usage arrived (ADR 0031). Absent means reported.

RemoteGenerationReceipt.description: Mirror of the core `GenerationReceipt`: the adapter-reported fate of a request's generation and prompt-cache intent, so a remote host can tell an honored repeatability request from a silently dropped one.

RemoteLlmCallRecord.description: Wire mirror of one logical LLM call and every provider attempt it consumed.

code.description: The attempt's namespaced failure code (`<namespace>:<spelling>`). Pre-cutover rows carried `provider_code`/`adapter_code`/`refusal_code` columns instead; they decode with `code: None`.

origin.description: Exact LLM Provider route that minted the reasoning replay state.
Exact LLM Provider route that minted the opaque replay state.

RemoteProviderRouteIdentity.description: Exact configured LLM Provider route that owns opaque replay state.

endpoint.description: Stable routing metadata, not a secret-bearing URL. LLM Provider endpoints reject URL userinfo; paths and query strings remain visible in remote envelopes and traces and therefore must not carry secrets.

RemoteToolIntentKind.description:
Wire mirror of the core tool-intent kind set.

Deliberately spelled out rather than generated from `lash_sansio::tool_intent_variants!`: the version-bump gate projects this enum's literal text, so generating it would move the variant list out of the `REMOTE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` guard's sight. The two `From` impls in `core_conversions::turn_result` are generated from that list instead, so a variant added to the core set fails to compile until it is added here and the wire version is bumped (FIG-2994).

RemoteTurnInputApplication.description:
Stable identity proving an admitted input became canonical turn input.

This wire DTO intentionally contains no display text. `input_id` and `source_key` correlate to the admission receipt, while `turn_id` and `committed_message_id` identify the canonical conversation application.

StreamBlockIdentity.description:
Provider-minted identity of one streamed output block.

Minted by the provider adapter from provider facts: OpenAI `(item_id, summary_index)`, Anthropic content-block index, or a deterministic per-attempt ordinal for providers with no native notion. The id is opaque to hosts; ordering comes from `ordinal`, never from parsing `id`. Live and replayed streams emit identical identities.

id.description: Opaque provider-minted block key, stable within one response attempt.

item_id.description: The reasoning or message item this block belongs to, when the provider has one. N blocks may share one item's replay material.

ordinal.description: Per-attempt block ordinal assigned by the provider adapter.

StreamBlockKind.description:
Which render lane a streamed output block belongs to.

A *block* is the unit a host renders: one OpenAI reasoning summary part, one Anthropic `thinking`/`text` content block, or one ordinal run of thought/text for providers with no native notion. Blocks name their owning reasoning item or message item when the provider has one; several blocks may share one item's replay material.

oneOf.description: Reasoning summary ("thinking") text, kept separate from assistant response text.
